# Deep Dive: Global Energy, AI, and Chevron Analysis

Report 140 | Published 2024-07-07 | Evaluated 2026-11-07

[Original member article](https://www.lynalden.com/premium-2024-7-7/) | [Article index](README.md) | [Structured review](../data/reviews/140.json)

Energy infrastructure, AI demand, and Chevron resilience.

The strongest verified calls concern 2024 easing and later regulatory change. Energy-demand direction held in 2025, but slower growth and weaker Chevron profits limit the equity inference. Egypt financing proved more resilient than a simple dollar-shortage narrative. AI demand is genuinely long horizon.

**Coverage:** All blocks and chart inventory read. Covered liquidity, labor, Egypt energy/FX, bitcoin/Lightning, securities enforcement, AI power demand, hydrocarbons and portfolio construction.

### 140-C04

**Easing may reverse yen weakness.**

| Field | Assessment |
| --- | --- |
| Verdict | Mixed |
| Type | forecast |
| Horizon | Late 2024 or 2025 |
| Conditions | Fed cuts or expands |
| Author modality | possible |
| Asset or variable | yen-fed-easing-reversal |
| Source blocks | 19 |
| Thesis family | yen-fed-easing-reversal |

The trigger occurred. Yen strengthened from ¥160.73/$ on July 5 to ¥141.93 on September 18, but much of this preceded the first Fed cut. By December 31 it was back to ¥157.37 and ended 2025 at ¥156.80. An initial reversal occurred, persistence was weak, and attribution to Fed easing alone fails.

**Direction:** Observed components differ.

**Timing:** Late 2024 or 2025

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify the proposed causal mechanism.

**Reviewer confidence:** medium

**Next test:** No magnitude or persistence threshold was specified; do not convert this into a binary causal win.

**Outcome evidence:**

- [DEXJPUS observations](https://fred.stlouisfed.org/series/DEXJPUS) | FRED / originating agency | 2026-11-07 | Verified in the audit

Yen/USD: July 5 2024 160.73; September 18 141.93; December 31 157.37; December 31 2025 156.80. Latest downloaded vintage, capped November 7; not original-release vintage.

- [FOMC statement](https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20240918a.htm) | Federal Reserve | 2024-09-18 | Verified in the audit

First cut reduced target by 50 bp to 4.75-5%.

| Conditions | Not specified |
| Author modality | asserted |

Upcoming stagnation has no dated onset, duration or growth threshold. Latest-vintage real GDP growth of 3.6%, 3.2%, 2.4% annualized in 2024 Q2-Q4 contradicts an immediate stagnation reading, but no exact forecast event was defined. Positive growth does not demonstrate the claimed fiscal mechanism.

**Direction:** No exact resolution rule; disclosed sensitivity only.

**Timing:** No fixed deadline stated.

**Mechanism:** Outcome evidence does not independently identify the proposed causal mechanism.

**Next test:** Record exact future statements with defined onset and variables; do not retrofit a threshold.
